summary: preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload under it
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is obfuscated with hex-mangled identifiers and proxy-object string indirection that hides the strings 'bun', 'unzip', 'powershell', and the Bun release URL. On install it downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it with execFileSync against the sibling file math_init.js — a 727KB single-line string-array/rotate obfuscator bundle tagged '// @bun @bun-cjs'. Executing a bundled payload under a freshly downloaded second language runtime is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: the payload never runs under Node and is therefore invisible to scanners that only inspect Node-resolved code. The advertised package purpose is a small React/mobx feature-gates helper (roughly 100 lines in dist/); there is no legitimate reason for such a library to fetch a second runtime at preinstall time and use it to run an obfuscated blob. package.json has an empty author field and no repository URL, and the '@servicetitan' scope is consistent with an impersonation of the ServiceTitan namespace.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
